definition: SGLang (short for Structured Generation Language) is an open-source framework for programming and serving large language models and multimodal models.
details: It was introduced by researchers affiliated with LMSYS and other institutions as a system combining a Python-embedded language for structured generation with a runtime for high-throughput inference. The project is designed for low latency and high-throughput inference workloads, and its documentation describes support for features such as structured outputs, speculative decoding, continuous batching, quantization, and compatibility with OpenAI-style APIs.

explainer.lead: SGLang (Structured Generation Language) is an open-source framework for programming and serving large language and multimodal models. It combines a Python-embedded language for structured generation with a high-throughput runtime.

tiers.eli5: Like a toolkit for telling a model exactly what shape of answer to give, while also serving many users quickly.
tiers.practitioner: Designed for low latency and high throughput, with structured outputs, speculative decoding, continuous batching, quantization and OpenAI-style API compatibility. Pitfall: it is aimed at inference workloads, not a general training stack.
tiers.paperLevel: A system combining a Python-embedded structured generation language with a runtime for high-throughput inference; introduced by researchers affiliated with LMSYS and other institutions.

explainer.example: Serving a model with structured outputs and continuous batching behind an OpenAI-style API.
